Hierarchical Clustering: Examples and Exercises

This file contains 7 different examples of Hierarchical Clustering implementation,
demonstrating clustering, evaluation, tuning, validation, and model analysis.
Plus 10 exercises for practice.

Author: ML Curriculum
Date: 2024

sections.title: Example 1: Basic Hierarchical Clustering
sections.body:
```python
print("\nExample 1: Basic Hierarchical Clustering")
print("-" * 65)

# Generate synthetic data with clear clusters
np.random.seed(42)
n_samples = 200
n_features = 2
n_clusters = 4

X, true_labels = make_blobs(
    n_samples=n_samples,
    n_features=n_features,
    centers=n_clusters,
    cluster_std=1.0,
    random_state=42,
)

print(f"Dataset shape: {X.shape}")
print(f"Number of clusters: {n_clusters}")

# Basic Hierarchical Clustering
hierarchical_basic = AgglomerativeClustering(
    n_clusters=n_clusters, linkage="ward", distance_threshold=None
)

hierarchical_basic.fit(X)
labels = hierarchical_basic.labels_

print(f"\nHierarchical Clustering Results:")
print(f"Number of clusters: {len(np.unique(labels))}")
print(f"Cluster labels: {np.unique(labels)}")

# Evaluation metrics
silhouette_avg = silhouette_score(X, labels)
calinski_avg = calinski_harabasz_score(X, labels)
davies_avg = davies_bouldin_score(X, labels)

print(f"\nEvaluation Metrics:")
print(f"Silhouette Score: {silhouette_avg:.4f}")
print(f"Calinski-Harabasz Index: {calinski_avg:.4f}")
print(f"Davies-Bouldin Index: {davies_avg:.4f}")

# Cluster analysis
unique_labels = np.unique(labels)
print(f"\nCluster Analysis:")
for label in unique_labels:
    cluster_size = np.sum(labels == label)
    cluster_percentage = (cluster_size / len(labels)) * 100
    print(f"Cluster {label}: {cluster_size} points ({cluster_percentage:.1f}%)")

joblib.dump(hierarchical_basic, "models/hierarchical_example1_basic.pkl")
print("Basic Hierarchical Clustering model saved to: models/")
```

sections.title: Example 2: Different Linkage Methods
sections.body:
```python
print("\n\nExample 2: Different Linkage Methods")
print("-" * 70)

# Generate data for comparison
np.random.seed(42)
X_comp = make_blobs(n_samples=300, n_features=2, centers=3, random_state=42)[0]

# Compare different linkage methods
linkage_methods = ["ward", "complete", "average", "single"]
results = {}

print("Comparing Different Linkage Methods:")
print("-" * 60)
print(f"{'Linkage':<12s} {'Clusters':<10s} {'Silhouette':<12s} {'Calinski':<12s}")
print("-" * 60)

for method in linkage_methods:
    hierarchical = AgglomerativeClustering(
        n_clusters=3, linkage=method, distance_threshold=None
    )

    hierarchical.fit(X_comp)
    labels = hierarchical.labels_

    silhouette = silhouette_score(X_comp, labels)
    calinski = calinski_harabasz_score(X_comp, labels)

    results[method] = {
        "silhouette": silhouette,
        "calinski": calinski,
        "model": hierarchical,
    }

    print(
        f"{method:<12s} {len(np.unique(labels)):<10d} {silhouette:<12.4f} {calinski:<12.4f}"
    )

best_method = max(results.keys(), key=lambda x: results[x]["silhouette"])
print(f"\nBest method (highest silhouette): {best_method}")

joblib.dump(
    results[best_method]["model"], "models/hierarchical_example2_best_linkage.pkl"
)
print(f"Best model ({best_method}) saved to: models/")
```

sections.title: Example 3: Dendrogram Analysis
sections.body:
```python
print("\n\nExample 3: Dendrogram Analysis")
print("-" * 70)

# Generate data for dendrogram
np.random.seed(42)
X_dendro = make_blobs(n_samples=50, n_features=2, centers=3, random_state=42)[0]

print(f"Dendrogram dataset shape: {X_dendro.shape}")

# Create linkage matrix
linkage_matrix = linkage(X_dendro, method="ward", metric="euclidean")

print(f"\nLinkage Matrix Shape: {linkage_matrix.shape}")
print(f"First few rows of linkage matrix:")
print(linkage_matrix[:5])

# Calculate cophenetic correlation
original_distances = pdist(X_dendro)
cophenetic_distances = cophenet(linkage_matrix)
cophenetic_correlation = np.corrcoef(original_distances, cophenetic_distances)[0, 1]

print(f"\nCophenetic Correlation: {cophenetic_correlation:.4f}")

# Analyze dendrogram structure
print(f"\nDendrogram Analysis:")
print(f"Number of merges: {len(linkage_matrix)}")
print(
    f"Height range: {linkage_matrix[:, 2].min():.4f} to {linkage_matrix[:, 2].max():.4f}"
)

# Find optimal number of clusters using dendrogram
# For demonstration, we'll use a simple approach
heights = linkage_matrix[:, 2]
height_diffs = np.diff(heights)
optimal_cutoff_idx = np.argmax(height_diffs) + 1
optimal_height = heights[optimal_cutoff_idx]

print(f"Suggested cut-off height: {optimal_height:.4f}")

# Get clusters at different heights
clusters_2 = fcluster(linkage_matrix, 2, criterion="maxclust")
clusters_3 = fcluster(linkage_matrix, 3, criterion="maxclust")
clusters_4 = fcluster(linkage_matrix, 4, criterion="maxclust")

print(f"\nClusters at different levels:")
print(f"2 clusters: {len(np.unique(clusters_2))}")
print(f"3 clusters: {len(np.unique(clusters_3))}")
print(f"4 clusters: {len(np.unique(clusters_4))}")
```

sections.title: Example 4: Distance Threshold Clustering
sections.body:
```python
print("\n\nExample 4: Distance Threshold Clustering")
print("-" * 70)

# Generate data with different cluster densities
np.random.seed(42)
X_threshold = make_blobs(
    n_samples=400, n_features=2, centers=4, cluster_std=1.5, random_state=42
)[0]

print(f"Distance threshold dataset shape: {X_threshold.shape}")

# Test different distance thresholds
distance_thresholds = [0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5]
results_threshold = {}

print("Testing Different Distance Thresholds:")
print("-" * 60)
print(f"{'Threshold':<12s} {'Clusters':<10s} {'Silhouette':<12s} {'Calinski':<12s}")
print("-" * 60)

for threshold in distance_thresholds:
    hierarchical = AgglomerativeClustering(
        n_clusters=None, linkage="ward", distance_threshold=threshold
    )

    hierarchical.fit(X_threshold)
    labels = hierarchical.labels_

    if len(np.unique(labels)) > 1:  # Need at least 2 clusters for metrics
        silhouette = silhouette_score(X_threshold, labels)
        calinski = calinski_harabasz_score(X_threshold, labels)
    else:
        silhouette = 0
        calinski = 0

    results_threshold[threshold] = {
        "n_clusters": len(np.unique(labels)),
        "silhouette": silhouette,
        "calinski": calinski,
        "model": hierarchical,
    }

    print(
        f"{threshold:<12.1f} {len(np.unique(labels)):<10d} {silhouette:<12.4f} {calinski:<12.4f}"
    )

# Find best threshold
best_threshold = max(
    results_threshold.keys(),
    key=lambda x: (
        results_threshold[x]["silhouette"]
        if results_threshold[x]["n_clusters"] > 1
        else 0
    ),
)

print(f"\nBest threshold (highest silhouette): {best_threshold}")

joblib.dump(
    results_threshold[best_threshold]["model"],
    "models/hierarchical_example4_best_threshold.pkl",
)
print(f"Best model (threshold={best_threshold}) saved to: models/")
```

sections.title: Example 5: Hierarchical Clustering with Feature Scaling
sections.body:
```python
print("\n\nExample 5: Hierarchical Clustering with Feature Scaling")
print("-" * 75)

# Generate data with different scales
np.random.seed(42)
n_samples = 300

# Create features with different scales
feature1 = np.random.normal(0, 1, n_samples)  # Scale ~1
feature2 = np.random.normal(0, 100, n_samples)  # Scale ~100
feature3 = np.random.normal(0, 0.01, n_samples)  # Scale ~0.01

X_unscaled = np.column_stack([feature1, feature2, feature3])

# Add some clustering structure
X_unscaled[:100, 0] += 5
X_unscaled[100:200, 1] += 200
X_unscaled[200:300, 2] += 0.05

print("Feature scales before scaling:")
print(
    f"Feature 1: mean={X_unscaled[:, 0].mean():.4f}, std={X_unscaled[:, 0].std():.4f}"
)
print(
    f"Feature 2: mean={X_unscaled[:, 1].mean():.4f}, std={X_unscaled[:, 1].std():.4f}"
)
print(
    f"Feature 3: mean={X_unscaled[:, 2].mean():.4f}, std={X_unscaled[:, 2].std():.4f}"
)

# Hierarchical Clustering without scaling
hierarchical_unscaled = AgglomerativeClustering(n_clusters=3, linkage="ward")
hierarchical_unscaled.fit(X_unscaled)
labels_unscaled = hierarchical_unscaled.labels_

# Hierarchical Clustering with scaling
scaler = StandardScaler()
X_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_unscaled)

hierarchical_scaled = AgglomerativeClustering(n_clusters=3, linkage="ward")
hierarchical_scaled.fit(X_scaled)
labels_scaled = hierarchical_scaled.labels_

print(f"\nFeature scales after scaling:")
print(f"Feature 1: mean={X_scaled[:, 0].mean():.4f}, std={X_scaled[:, 0].std():.4f}")
print(f"Feature 2: mean={X_scaled[:, 1].mean():.4f}, std={X_scaled[:, 1].std():.4f}")
print(f"Feature 3: mean={X_scaled[:, 2].mean():.4f}, std={X_scaled[:, 2].std():.4f}")

# Compare results
print(f"\nComparison of Results:")
print("-" * 50)
print(f"{'Method':<15s} {'Silhouette':<12s} {'Calinski':<12s}")
print("-" * 50)

silhouette_unscaled = silhouette_score(X_unscaled, labels_unscaled)
calinski_unscaled = calinski_harabasz_score(X_unscaled, labels_unscaled)
print(f"{'Unscaled':<15s} {silhouette_unscaled:<12.4f} {calinski_unscaled:<12.4f}")

silhouette_scaled = silhouette_score(X_scaled, labels_scaled)
calinski_scaled = calinski_harabasz_score(X_scaled, labels_scaled)
print(f"{'Scaled':<15s} {silhouette_scaled:<12.4f} {calinski_scaled:<12.4f}")

joblib.dump(hierarchical_scaled, "models/hierarchical_example5_scaled.pkl")
print("Scaled Hierarchical Clustering model saved to: models/")
```

sections.title: Example 6: Hierarchical Clustering Limitations
sections.body:
```python
print("\n\nExample 6: Hierarchical Clustering Limitations")
print("-" * 75)

# Generate challenging datasets
np.random.seed(42)

# Dataset 1: Non-spherical clusters (moons)
X_moons, _ = make_moons(n_samples=200, noise=0.1, random_state=42)

# Dataset 2: Concentric circles
X_circles, _ = make_circles(n_samples=200, noise=0.1, factor=0.5, random_state=42)

# Dataset 3: Uneven cluster sizes
X_uneven = make_blobs(n_samples=[30, 150, 30], centers=3, random_state=42)[0]

datasets = {"Moons": X_moons, "Circles": X_circles, "Uneven": X_uneven}

print("Hierarchical Clustering Performance on Challenging Datasets:")
print("-" * 75)
print(
    f"{'Dataset':<12s} {'Linkage':<10s} {'Clusters':<10s} {'Silhouette':<12s} {'Comment':<20s}"
)
print("-" * 75)

for name, X_data in datasets.items():
    for linkage_method in ["ward", "complete", "average"]:
        hierarchical = AgglomerativeClustering(n_clusters=2, linkage=linkage_method)

        hierarchical.fit(X_data)
        labels = hierarchical.labels_

        silhouette = silhouette_score(X_data, labels)

        if name == "Moons":
            comment = "Non-spherical shapes"
        elif name == "Circles":
            comment = "Concentric circles"
        else:
            comment = "Uneven sizes"

        print(
            f"{name:<12s} {linkage_method:<10s} {len(np.unique(labels)):<10d} {silhouette:<12.4f} {comment:<20s}"
        )

print(f"\nKey Limitations Demonstrated:")
print("- Hierarchical clustering assumes similar cluster sizes")
print("- Sensitive to noise and outliers")
print("- Computationally expensive for large datasets")
print("- May not handle complex cluster shapes well")
```

sections.title: Example 7: Comprehensive Hierarchical Analysis
sections.body:
```python
print("\n\nExample 7: Comprehensive Hierarchical Analysis")
print("-" * 75)

# Generate comprehensive dataset
np.random.seed(42)
X_comprehensive = make_blobs(
    n_samples=500, n_features=3, centers=5, cluster_std=1.2, random_state=42
)[0]

# Add some noise
X_comprehensive += np.random.normal(0, 0.1, X_comprehensive.shape)

print(f"Comprehensive dataset shape: {X_comprehensive.shape}")

# Scale the data
scaler = StandardScaler()
X_comprehensive_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_comprehensive)

# Test different linkage methods and cluster numbers
linkage_methods = ["ward", "complete", "average", "single"]
n_clusters_range = range(2, 8)
results_comprehensive = {}

print("Comprehensive Hierarchical Clustering Analysis:")
print("-" * 75)
print(
    f"{'Linkage':<10s} {'Clusters':<10s} {'Silhouette':<12s} {'Calinski':<12s} {'Davies':<12s}"
)
print("-" * 75)

for method in linkage_methods:
    results_comprehensive[method] = {}

    for n_clusters in n_clusters_range:
        hierarchical = AgglomerativeClustering(n_clusters=n_clusters, linkage=method)

        hierarchical.fit(X_comprehensive_scaled)
        labels = hierarchical.labels_

        silhouette = silhouette_score(X_comprehensive_scaled, labels)
        calinski = calinski_harabasz_score(X_comprehensive_scaled, labels)
        davies = davies_bouldin_score(X_comprehensive_scaled, labels)

        results_comprehensive[method][n_clusters] = {
            "silhouette": silhouette,
            "calinski": calinski,
            "davies": davies,
            "model": hierarchical,
        }

        print(
            f"{method:<10s} {n_clusters:<10d} {silhouette:<12.4f} {calinski:<12.4f} {davies:<12.4f}"
        )

# Find best configuration
best_silhouette = 0
best_config = None

for method in linkage_methods:
    for n_clusters in n_clusters_range:
        silhouette = results_comprehensive[method][n_clusters]["silhouette"]
        if silhouette > best_silhouette:
            best_silhouette = silhouette
            best_config = (method, n_clusters)

best_method, best_n_clusters = best_config
best_model = results_comprehensive[best_method][best_n_clusters]["model"]

print(f"\nBest Configuration:")
print(f"Linkage Method: {best_method}")
print(f"Number of Clusters: {best_n_clusters}")
print(f"Silhouette Score: {best_silhouette:.4f}")

# Final model analysis
final_labels = best_model.labels_
unique_labels = np.unique(final_labels)

print(f"\nFinal Model Analysis:")
print(f"Number of clusters: {len(unique_labels)}")

# Cluster analysis
print(f"\nCluster Distribution:")
for label in unique_labels:
    cluster_size = np.sum(final_labels == label)
    cluster_percentage = (cluster_size / len(final_labels)) * 100
    print(f"Cluster {label}: {cluster_size} points ({cluster_percentage:.1f}%)")

joblib.dump(best_model, "models/hierarchical_example7_comprehensive.pkl")
print("Comprehensive Hierarchical Clustering model saved to: models/")

# Summary
print("\n" + "=" * 80)
print("HIERARCHICAL CLUSTERING COMPREHENSIVE EXAMPLES - SUMMARY")
print("=" * 80)

print("\nExamples Covered:")
print("1. Basic Hierarchical Clustering")
print("2. Different Linkage Methods")

print("4. Distance Threshold Clustering")

print("6. Hierarchical Clustering Limitations")
```
